question: Then do I lose all the traffic?  any remedy?

answers: No, you would not lose all the traffic. Since multiple policies can be applied to a protocol, a priority is associated with each policy.  Policies with the lowest set priority are evaluated first. Then the next lowest policy on the priority list is evaluated. If there are no policies associated with a front-end port, the system will redirect the traffic to the default pool, which is the pool that was configured when the basic load balancer was deployed. To avoid this situation, make sure to define and associate appropriate policies with the front-end port to handle the traffic according to your requirements.

I don't have specific information on the security implications of configuring non-HTTP/HTTPS traffic for global load balancers.
What exactly the global load balancers do and any subscription  available?

Global load balancers help distribute network or application traffic across multiple locations or regions. IBM Cloud Internet Services (CIS) is an example of a global load balancer provider, offering features like Global Load Balancer (GLB), Caching, Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Page rules. They help to ensure reliability and performance by directing traffic to the most available and responsive endpoints. As for subscriptions, IBM CIS offers various plans, including a Free Trial plan with limited features and Standard paid plans with additional capabilities. You can refer to the IBM Cloud website for the most current and detailed information on their subscription options.
How frequently do you do a health check in the back-end? and is there any limitations?

Health checks in IBM Cloud Internet Services (CIS) are done periodically to monitor the availability of origin servers. The frequency of these health checks is every 15 seconds. However, the default retry rate is 5 retries per second, which can be configured. It is not recommended to increase the retry rate significantly as retries use exponential backoff.
Regarding limitations, it is important to note that health checks for deleted pools and origins cannot be filtered, but they still appear in the table. Also, when adding the request header name for a health check, use 'Host' with a capitalized 'H'. Using a lower-case 'host' for a health check will fail.
how do you distribute among bare-metal and virtual-server instances?  Multiple policies ok?

The IBM Cloud Load Balancer service distributes traffic among multiple server instances, including bare-metal and virtual-server instances, by using Layer 7 (application layer) data. Layer 7 load balancing is supported for HTTP and HTTPS traffic only. Multiple policies can be associated with a front-end port, and these policies are evaluated in order, based on the priority assigned to each policy. Each Layer 7 rule is associated with a policy, and if all the rules that are associated with the policy evaluate to true, the policy is matched, so the associated action is taken.
For more information, see [L7 Policy and Rules](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/loadbalancer-service?topic=loadbalancer-service-layer-7-policy).

If you refer to the scenario where multiple policies are not associated with a front-end port in the IBM Cloud Load Balancer service, then the system might not be able to apply the appropriate actions to the data traffic.

How do I change the email address that is used for MFA? 

You can update the email address that is used for MFA on the [Verification methods and authentication factors](https://iam.cloud.ibm.com/mysecurity) page. From the Authentication factors section, click Show authentication factors > Add. Select Email-based and enter the email address where you want to receive OTPs as an authentication factor. Then, enter the OTP you receive to confirm your choice. Next, click Complete. After you add the new factor, select the old email address, and click Remove.





 Can trusted profiles create user API keys? 

If you use a trusted profile, you can't create a user API key. You can still create and manage all other API keys. For example, service ID API keys.

To create a user API key, your IAM ID and the IAM ID of the user that's requesting the user API key must be the same. When you apply a trusted profile, you take on the IAM ID of that profile.

Layer 7 load balancing 

Both public and private application load balancers support layer 7 load balancing. Data traffic is distributed based on configured policies and rules. A policy defines the action to take, which means how the traffic is distributed, when the incoming request matches the rules that are associated with the policy.



 Policies 

You can define policies for HTTP and HTTPS listeners. For each policy, you must define one or more rules. The policy is applied only when all its rules are matched.

You can attach more than one policy to a listener. In general, a policy with the lowest priority is evaluated first. Each policy must have a different priority.

If the incoming request does not match the rules for any policy, the system request redirects to the configured HTTPS redirect listener, if present. Otherwise, the system redirects the request to the default pool of the listener. The HTTPS redirect has a higher precedence over the default pool on an HTTP listener.
